text: Everything built in Chapters 2 through 5 secured and protected OverlookDB as it already exists. But Overlook's real appointment scheduling doesn't happen only inside this database — a separate, existing booking platform is where new appointments actually get created first.

For OverlookDB to stay useful for reporting and billing, those appointments need to land in it on an ongoing basis, not as a one-time import. Lesson 2 planned this as the capstone's fifth piece from the start. A manual export-and-import process would be exactly the kind of person-dependent work Lesson 1's mandate exists to eliminate — Azure Data Factory moves this data on a schedule instead.

This is built last, in Chapter 6, for a real reason: the pipeline needs somewhere stable, secured, and protected to write into. Building it before infrastructure, security, or HA/DR existed would mean writing into nothing, or into an unsecured, unprotected target.
A perfectly secured database that never receives new data isn't solving a real problem — it's a museum piece. Next lesson builds the real pipeline moving appointment data into OverlookDB.
